guidebook.span_sentence: Non-smokers exposed to second-hand smoke at home showed significantly higher urinary cotinine levels.

triad.description: BERT proposed an incorrect LSF category (Environmental_exposures), and the LLM uncritically adopted BERT's error instead of correcting to Ground Truth (Substance_use).

guidebook.guideline: Passive, involuntary, or second-hand tobacco exposures, smoke residues, and chemical markers of tobacco combustion (e.g., ETS, second-hand smoke, environmental tobacco smoke, nicotine markers) belong strictly to Substance_use due to tobacco-product ontology precedence, rather than Environmental_exposures.

guidebook.span_sentence: Mental health outcomes and behavioral interventions were assessed in sexually abused children.

triad.description: BERT proposed the correct category (Socioeconomic_factors), but the LLM incorrectly rejected it as Non-LSF by treating adverse childhood trauma as an excluded demographic cohort.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Socioeconomic_factors on spans describing adverse childhood experiences, interpersonal maltreatment, or household trauma (e.g., sexually abused children, childhood physical abuse, domestic violence exposure, severe child neglect), confirm BERT and preserve Socioeconomic_factors; do not override to O under demographic filtering rules, as interpersonal and household trauma constitutes an established social determinant of health rather than an unmodifiable demographic attribute.

triad.description: BERT proposed Environmental_exposures due to ambient emission modifiers, and the Generator uncritically adopted it instead of classifying the residential built-environment head as Socioeconomic_factors.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Environmental_exposures on complex noun phrases whose primary semantic head denotes a residential, community, or geographic environment (e.g., urban area, residential zone, rural district) modified by ambient exposure sources, override BERT and label as Socioeconomic_factors; preserve Environmental_exposures only when the span's primary nominal head directly denotes the physical pollutant, hazard, or exposure agent itself (e.g., outdoor emissions, particulate matter).

guidebook.span_sentence: Agricultural wastewater and returning water affect regional water quality and environmental exposure risks.

triad.description: BERT correctly proposed Environmental_exposures for ambient water media and pollution hazards, but the LLM erroneously rejected them as Non-LSF due to over-filtering on agricultural/ecological study contexts.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Environmental_exposures on environmental quality parameters, pollution hazards, or ambient water media (e.g., water quality, agricultural wastewater, effluent runoff), confirm BERT and preserve Environmental_exposures; do not override to Non-LSF (O) on the grounds that the abstract describes agricultural, ecological, or physical systems without explicit human subjects, as ambient water media and contamination factors intrinsically constitute environmental exposures.

guidebook.span_sentence: VOC sorption and emission dynamics of gypsum board in indoor environments.

triad.description: BERT correctly predicted Environmental_exposures for an indoor emission substrate/sink, but the Generator over-filtered it to Non-LSF (O) as an inert physical object.

guidebook.guideline: When BERT predicts Environmental_exposures on indoor building materials, structural substrates, or emission surfaces (e.g., gypsum board, wall linings, flooring materials) within an indoor air or pollutant transfer context, confirm BERT and preserve Environmental_exposures; do not override to O as inert objects, because structural materials functioning as contaminant sinks or emission sources constitute valid environmental exposure pathway components.
